identity: An Arabic Islamic-studies general-knowledge multiple-choice quiz, 20 items, options unlabelled. Every <NL>-delimited block is one complete MCQ: a short interrogative stem followed by its answer choices, four choices in every item except item 2 (the tajwid item), which has the three canonical rulings of the miim saakinah. There is no running prose anywhere in the document. The whole text is layout, and the layout is stem slots and option slots. Register §S of my doctrine, with §J6 as the nearest cousin.
law: The unit is the layout slot, not the sentence. Structure per item: [stem, including every honorific, every Quranic quotation and every forward-referring phrase such as الأدوات الآتية] then one segment per option. The stem is ONE segment however long; each option is ONE segment however short. Single-word options do split (precedent: صح ‖ خطأ ‖ and غيرصحيح ‖ صحيح ‖), and a personal name of the form X بن Y never splits internally. LAW 3 (comma-lists and appositions weld) governs the inside of a stem but does NOT reach answer options, because options are list items occupying separate layout slots, and LAW 0-prime counts a list-item break as a boundary mark. Free boundaries: the token immediately before each of the 20 <NL> tokens, and the final token.
reasoning: Step zero was register identification and it decided almost everything. Twenty interrogative stems, each trailed by parallel answer choices, each block closed by <NL>. That is §S, whose two source documents are my highest-scoring in the file (F1 93.5 and 98.0) and where every single error I made was a cut INSIDE a stem, never a failure to cut between options. So options split and stems do not. The systemic risk I weighed and rejected was reading a whole <NL> block as one segment (the §T one-balloon-one-segment analogue); rejected because §S1 gold ends the stem before the first option (علوم اللغة العربية هو ‖ العلوم الإنسانية والاجتماعية ‖ العلوم التطبيقية ‖) and §J6 gold splits even one-word options (وترتديه النساء ‖ صح ‖ خطأ ‖). --- HARD SITE 1, item 2 at index 26. Is the Quranic quotation إن كنتم صادقين inside the stem or its own unit? Inside. Direct precedent: gold علام يدل قوله تعالى ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة ‖ عدم القرب من الشجرة — قوله تعالى plus its quotation welds and the boundary lands at the END of the quotation. So the cut is at صادقين and the three tajwid terms are three options. Marked med: it is the only stem here carrying embedded scripture, and it leans on A4, the colon after صادقين being a layout colon introducing options rather than a prose colon. --- HARD SITE 2, item 4 at 59 through 63. أي أداة من الأدوات الآتية قام قابيل بقتل أخيه هابيل بواسطتها is exactly the shape that cost me five false cuts in doc_1c49614cd6bc, where الأمثلة الآتية was followed by examples that welded into the stem. It resolves the other way here: in that document the real options came after هو, so the listed examples were stem-internal, whereas in this item فأس / فك الحمار / سكين / عصا غليظة are the only candidates for options and nothing follows them before <NL>. Welding them would leave this item with zero option boundaries while its 19 siblings have three or four. The document is its own strongest evidence, so I cut. I marked 60 and 62 med because the internal grouping is the least regular in the file: فك الحمار is a two-token option flanked by one-token فأس and سكين, and a reading of فأس فك الحمار as a single phrase would yield only three options. I take the four-option reading because عصا غليظة is unambiguously noun-plus-adjective and every sibling item has four. --- HARD SITE 3, the honorific tails, worth eight boundaries. Items 1, 9, 15 and 17 end their STEMS with عليه السلام or صلى الله عليه وسلم, while item 6 instead puts عليه السلام at the end of every OPTION. Per A1 an honorific never separates from the name it modifies, so it simply stays on whichever side its name is on: stem-final at 7, 146, 265 and 308, option-final at 90, 93, 96 and 99. Reading item 6 the other way would have misplaced four boundaries by three tokens each. --- HARD SITE 4, items 16 and 18 are the same question printed twice, once with بأسد joined at 281 and once with ب أسد split across 322 and 323. An orthographically detached preposition is not a boundary, exactly as ب المر at 72 and 73 in item 5 is not; both stems end at الغالب, and item 5 ends at المر. --- The remainder is mechanical. Proper names of the form X بن Y are one token-group and never split, which fixes every three- and four-token option (including حمزة بن عبد المطلب at 352 to 355 and السيدة أم كلثوم at 313 to 315). The repeated lexical head of each option marks each option start: يوم in item 1, سورة in item 5, معجزة recurring at 149 in item 9, السيدة in item 17. One near-trap in item 15: بركة بنت ثعلبة and أم أيمن are the same woman, but the quiz lists them as separate options, so they are separate segments regardless. My default posture stayed LAW 0-double-prime, weld unless I can name the mark, and here I can name it at every one of the 99 sites; the mark is a layout slot rather than a full stop. Final tally: 20 stem boundaries plus 79 option boundaries equals 99, of which 20 are the free pre-<NL> and final positions.
